ra: The shayatin are the rebellious/evil class of jinn in Islamic cosmology.
Classical lore (al-Jahiz, al-Damiri) enumerates the ghul among the classes of jinn.
The si'lat is listed among the classes of jinn in classical Arabian demonology.
In Persianate Islamic tradition the div is assimilated to the jinn (a regional classification).
The ifrit is a standard powerful subtype in the classical jinn taxonomy (wiring the existing entity).
The marid is a standard rebellious/powerful subtype in the classical jinn taxonomy (wiring the existing entity).
Iblis (al-Shaytan al-rajim) is the chief of the devils; the shayatin are his host and instruments of temptation.
The defining function of the shayatin is whispering temptation and deception (waswasa).
The dybbuk is broadly reckoned among harmful spirits/demons (shedim) in Jewish folk demonology, though it originates from a dead human soul.
The dybbuk manifests as affliction/illness of the possessed host requiring exorcism.
Ibbur (benevolent righteous indwelling) is the structural and moral counterpart to the dybbuk (malevolent possession) in Lurianic Kabbalah.
In the dominant legend the golem is fashioned as a protector and servant of the Jewish community.
The estrie is a female demon of medieval Jewish folklore, classed among the harmful demonic beings (shedim).
Gog and Magog embody the final eschatological assault and devastation in Ezekiel 38-39 and Revelation 20.
